sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Initial Assessment in Pregnancy
sections.description: This section details the patient's demographic profile, chief complaints, and the initial physical and laboratory findings. It establishes the clinical context of managing a complex abdominal mass in a high-risk pregnancy (maternal age >40, obesity) and introduces the challenge of distinguishing between obstetric and non-obstetric pathology.
subtopics: Patient demographics and risk factors (nulliparity, advanced maternal age, BMI)
Symptomatology: Acute abdominal pain, dyspnea, and mechanical compression effects
Physical examination findings: Abdominal distension disproportionate to gestational age
Bimanual examination results: Identification of fixed pelvic masses
Initial vital signs and exclusion of cardiac/pulmonary causes
Laboratory interpretation: Distinguishing pregnancy-related leukocytosis from infection vs. malignancy

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Imaging Strategy and Differential Diagnosis
sections.description: This section explores the multimodal imaging approach required when standard anatomy is obscured by a gravid uterus. It analyzes the utility of ultrasound versus non-contrast MRI in characterizing large masses, interpreting tumor markers within the unique physiology of pregnancy, and formulating a differential diagnosis between degenerating leiomyomas and decidualized endometriomas.
subtopics: Limitations of physical exam in late second trimester with large masses
Role of Color Doppler Ultrasound: Identifying vascularity and cystic components
Indications for Non-Contrast MRI: Safety protocols and superiority in defining tissue planes
Interpretation of CA-125 in pregnancy: Physiological fluctuations vs. pathological elevation
Differentiating decidualized endometriomas from cystic degenerating leiomyomas on imaging
Assessing the 'steric bulk' impact on organ displacement (diaphragm compression)

sections.description: This section outlines the multidisciplinary risk-benefit analysis leading to surgical intervention during pregnancy. It details the operative strategy, including the decision to remove only the symptomatic/critical mass while leaving others in situ, anesthesia considerations, fetal monitoring techniques, and specific pharmacological prophylaxis used to maintain pregnancy stability.
subtopics: Criteria for surgery during pregnancy: Rupture risk, torsion, infection, and refractory symptoms
Multidisciplinary consensus: Balancing maternal safety with fetal preservation
Intraoperative fetal monitoring protocols (continuous heart rate documentation)
Surgical approach selection: Laparotomy vs. Laparoscopy based on mass size and location
Intraoperative findings: Pedunculated twisted leiomyoma with ischemic necrosis
Surgical technique: Partial myomectomy strategy to minimize uterine trauma

sections.section_title: Postoperative Care, Obstetric Course, and Delivery Planning
sections.description: This section covers the immediate postoperative recovery focusing on anemia management and infection control. It tracks the obstetric follow-up regarding fetal growth relative to maternal mass reduction and discusses the strategic planning for delivery mode based on residual pelvic anatomy.
subtopics: Management of post-operative anemia: Iron supplementation strategies in pregnancy
Antibiotic stewardship tailored to urine cultures (Klebsiella pneumoniae) during pregnancy
Hormonal prophylaxis regimen (Progesterone/Hydroxyprogesterone) for preventing preterm labor
Fetal surveillance outcomes: Growth percentiles and amniotic fluid indices post-surgery
Determining mode of delivery: Indications for elective Cesarean section due to pelvic obstruction
